title: Choose the visual world for Track & Trace
question: The roll assigned Trains at a Glance. Keep it, take the pick or the alternate, re-roll safer or bolder, or take the category standard.

options.label: Trains at a Glance
options.lineage: Indian Railways' printed timetable: the annual book on every station bookstall and the ruled timetable posters on platform walls
options.thesis: Your PNR is one row in the railway's own timetable: set in columns, ruled, and footnoted with where every figure came from.
options.viewport: A ruled sheet fills the viewport. A title strip sets the product name like a table heading. The PNR entry is the first ruled row: ten numeral cells in 3-3-4 with a hairline between groups and 'Check status' as the row's action. Beneath, the three assurances are set as footnotes with dagger marks. On a phone the sheet is portrait and the row spans the screen.
options.risk: Density can become a wall on a phone; every table must reflow to labelled rows, and the numeral columns need real tabular figures or the world reads as a spreadsheet.

raised.raise: Colour lives only in band edges and status pills; the text field stays achromatic.
The ten-digit row is one unbroken line that scales and never wraps, and the request lifecycle shows a moving 'now' mark.
Provenance and the not-affiliated notice are set as a designed agate foot on every result, small print as content.
One accent role, spent only on the primary action; status colours stay semantic.
Every control is built from the sheet's own material (ruled cells, footnote marks, column heads), never a stock widget.

regions.label: three ruled columns: how it works

options.label: Station Name Board
options.lineage: The yellow enamel station boards with black bilingual lettering and the height-above-sea-level line, read from a moving train
options.thesis: Every station announces itself the same way, and so does every status: a black-bordered board, one fact, two scripts, legible at speed.
options.viewport: A yellow board fills the first screen with the product name in black block letters. Below the border, the PNR entry is a black slab with ten yellow cells. Status boards stack as you scroll, each carrying exactly one fact.
options.risk: Yellow saturates fast and collides with the amber warning role; the board form can flatten a dense passenger table into a poster. It is also the familiar destination for this category's bolder runs.

options.label: Variable Type Specimen
options.thesis: The status is the specimen: one giant status word, every detail in tiny mono labels.
options.viewport: A grid of ten PNR digits at display size; after the check the status word sets enormous while mono readouts list train, date, and provenance.
options.case: Holds clarity: hierarchy by scale alone and a strict baseline grid make the status readable from across a platform. Loses identification: no traveler reads their ticket as a type specimen.
options.risk: A typographic conceit that leaves journey data as a footnote.

options.label: Rhythm Machine Step Row
options.thesis: The PNR is sixteen keys under a chase light; the check runs when the light comes round.
options.viewport: A single unbroken row of ten keys across the screen; typing arms keys, submit sweeps a chase light through validation, source, and result.
options.case: The ten-key row is a striking entry, but lit keys on charcoal drift straight back into the dark console this redesign leaves behind.
options.kept: One unbroken row that scales instead of wrapping, with a visible 'now' mark.
options.risk: Playful hardware tone for a document people read under stress.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.lineage: diffraction at a forming cloud edge
options.thesis: An achromatic sheet with colour only at the hairline edge of the status band.
options.viewport: Wide white margins, thin humanist type, a narrow mint-rose-violet fringe along the status band edge.
options.case: Thin humanist type fails on a sunlit platform, and no traveler identifies with a cloud edge.
options.kept: Colour confined to band edges while the text field stays achromatic.
options.risk: Too quiet to persuade and too thin to read in daylight.

options.label: Accretion Disk Threshold
options.thesis: Chart time as an event horizon: the ticket approaches, reddens, and either crosses or holds.
options.viewport: Concentric ring bands with the PNR at its current radius from chart time.
options.case: Concentric rings cannot carry a passenger table, and travelers do not identify with a horizon.
options.kept: One accent, spent on exactly one active element.
options.risk: Cosmic drama over plain railway facts.

options.label: Double-Feature One-Sheet
options.thesis: Two titles shouting over a collage, with a wall of agate at the foot.
options.viewport: A huge distressed title, a second half its size, promises wedged into corners, agate billing at the foot.
options.case: A shouting hierarchy contradicts an honesty product, and misregistration hurts numeral legibility.
options.kept: A designed agate foot that carries the small print as content.

options.label: Village Coffeehouse Identity
options.thesis: A woodcut mark over torn kraft, olive and terracotta, humanist caps letterspaced wide.
options.viewport: Torn-edge tiles as sections, a woodcut sun stamped in the header.
options.case: Torn kraft tiles and woodcut marks say artisan cafe, not railway, and tile edges eat data clarity.
options.kept: Total material commitment: every control is built from the world's own material.
options.risk: Nostalgia with no railway in it.

canonCard.label: Category standard
canonCard.thesis: The PNR checker this category ships, executed impeccably: a clean light utility page.
canonCard.viewport: A large PNR input on top, a status card below, a row of feature tiles, a footer.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
